subject: Interim caching partner added — escrow access & evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acme-analytics.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2027-05-12T09:13:00Z
Subject: Clarification on temporary caching partner and escrow access

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question on behalf of our security team — we noticed a short notice from your portal indicating an interim caching partner (EdgeRipple) will be used for a 3-week window in the us-east region for read-only prefix caching. Before we can approve this for production traffic, our reviewers need: 1) confirmation of the limited scope (read-only, no long-term storage), 2) an encryption-at-rest attestation for the partner, and 3) whether Redwood will provide audit log snapshots or escrow access while the partner is in place.

Can you confirm the above and share any attestation/document bundles? If you prefer, loop in the privacy or legal leads and we can book a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Elena
Security Program Manager
Acme Analytics

---
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi.Malhotra@redwood.com, Mina.Haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-12T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification on temporary caching partner and escrow access

Hi Elena — thanks for the flag. Short answers up front: the partner use is temporary (approx 3 weeks) and scope is read-cache only (no persistent tenant stores). We have an edge-level caching config that drops cached objects after 2 hours, and we will not route any PII to the partner beyond encrypted prefixes used for cache keys.

Attaching our current subprocessor matrix and the partner attestation we collected this morning. Rishi (privacy lead) and Mina (legal) are on copy to confirm the controls and to propose audit/escrow options.

Attachments: [attachment: subprocessor_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)], [attachment: edgecache-attestation-20270513.pdf (pdf)]

Proposed next steps:
- Rishi: confirm the technical mitigations are sufficient for Acme's bar.
- Mina: share suggested escrow/access wording (temporary, read-only, timeboxed).
- Elena: if acceptable, sign-off and we’ll provide a daily audit snapshot for the window.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---
From: Rishi.Malhotra@redwood.com <Rishi.Malhotra@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Mina.Haddad@redwood.com, Elena Soto <elena.soto@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification on temporary caching partner and escrow access

Thanks Kimberly. I reviewed the attestation and the matrix quickly — two follow-ups from privacy:
1) Can we confirm that the cache key derivation does not include raw customer content (we typically hash namespace + id; please confirm algorithm and salt handling).
2) For the audit snapshot: Acme requested escrow-style read-only access. Operationally we can provide daily signed audit logs (s3 access logs + request traces) and a rolling snapshot of cache metadata for the 3-week window. Would that satisfy their requirement or do they need live console access?

If Acme insists on console/escrow access we should scope a time-limited role with just read/list permissions and an RBAC token that expires. Mina — could you draft the temporary access clause and a short amendment to the DPA that covers the limited partner use and log escrow?

-Rishi
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

On 2027-05-12, Elena Soto wrote:
> Hi Kimberly,
>

---
From: Mina.Haddad@redwood.com <Mina.Haddad@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, Rishi.Malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification on temporary caching partner and escrow access

Thanks — drafting the clause now. Proposed language for the amendment (summary): Redwood may temporarily engage a third-party caching provider for no longer than 30 days per event; cached objects will be time-to-live limited (<=2 hours) and no customer content will be written to persistent storage by the partner. For escrow/audit we will provide daily signed log bundles and, where requested, time-limited read-only console tokens (scoped to audit logs only). DocuSign link for the one-off amendment will be shared if Acme requires an executed amendment.

Elena — please confirm whether the signed log bundles are acceptable or you require console tokens. If you need console tokens, share the exact principal name and window.

-Mina
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

---
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acme-analytics.com>
To: Mina.Haddad@redwood.com, Rishi.Malhotra@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-14T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification on temporary caching partner and escrow access

Thanks for the quick turnaround team — the attestation and proposed amendment look good. We prefer the signed daily log bundles rather than console tokens for now. Two final asks before we sign: 1) confirmation of the hashing algorithm used for cache keys (SHA-256 with per-tenant salt is acceptable), and 2) a DocuSign link for the temporary amendment so our procurement can execute.

If you can send the small cert on the hashing approach and the DocuSign URL I can push this through today.

Best,
Elena
Security Program Manager
Acme Analytics
